questions: When K > 1, must the chosen K elements be distinct indices, or can we choose the same element multiple times (e.g., choose A_i twice)?
For each i, are we to compute the maximum possible GCD over all choices of K elements that include A_i, or the GCD of some specific choice (like the first K elements including A_i)?
Does 'choose K elements from A' mean choose any K indices from 1..N, or must they be contiguous/subarray elements?
If multiple choices of K elements including A_i are possible, should we output a single GCD value (e.g., the GCD over all such choices combined) or one value per choice?
Is the GCD computed over the multiset of chosen values (including duplicates if allowed), or over the set of distinct values?
For each i, are we allowed to choose elements in any order, or does order matter for the GCD computation?
Should the output be printed as N space-separated integers on one line, or one per line?
If N=K, is the only choice the whole array, so the answer for each i is GCD(A_1,...,A_N)?
